title: The four-day week experiment
text: {{1}} recent years, hundreds of companies have trialled a four-day week, keeping full pay while fitting the same output into fewer hours. The idea {{2}} moved from radical experiment to mainstream policy discussion: trials in Britain and Iceland reported that staff felt {{3}} stress, took fewer sick days {{4}} before, and — the number that persuades finance directors — productivity held steady or even rose. Politicians {{5}} support the change argue that the five-day week is a relic of the industrial age, when hours and output moved together. {{6}} is not a universal cure: hospitals, {{7}} cannot simply close for an extra day, need different models, and some workers on compressed schedules report feeling rushed. Even so, the conversation has shifted, and the real debate now is {{8}} every job can fit into four days.

gaps.explanation: Present perfect with a singular subject: has moved.
Uncountable 'stress' and a reduction: felt less stress.

gaps.hint: pronoun: ___ is not a universal cure
gaps.explanation: 'It' refers to the idea as the subject.
Non-defining relative after the comma referring to hospitals.

gaps.hint: conjunction: the debate is ___ every job can fit
gaps.explanation: An indirect yes/no question after 'is': whether.
